_about: The /pathway page. Step values, evidence levels, findings and proposed actions. Numbers from brain notes/2026-11-14-0145-silta-deep-data-analysis.md, sources/2026-11-14-cancerregistry-screening-by-language.md, sources/2026-11-14-europepmc-unmet-need-and-access-by-origin.md. Levels: lang = measured by native language, ind = indirect (county, origin or all invitees), none = not measured. `charts` on a step lists chart modules from app/charts/ shown in that step's detail panel.

page.title: The gap opens at the door
page.lede: People whose native language is not Finnish, Swedish or Sámi get the same screening letter but attend about 20 points less often. After they attend, most of the gap closes. Most later steps are not reported by language at all. Select a step to see the evidence and what we propose.
notes: “Other native language” includes people whose native language is unknown. The registry does not split attendance by individual language.

Language, education and region of birth overlap. Across ~290 municipalities, language still predicts lower breast and colorectal attendance after controlling for education, age, urbanisation and unemployment; for cervical screening, unemployment explains the area differences. This is an area-level model and does not prove cause.
County waiting times were read from Cancer Registry charts (±0.1 month).

Sources: Finnish Cancer Registry mass-screening statistics, published 20 May 2026 (native language, region of birth, education, previous result, delays); National Cancer Strategy 2026–2035; THL Maamu 2010–12 and FinMonik 2018–19 surveys; Norway RCT; YouScreen (London); Community Guide. Captured sources and analysis: team knowledge base (madviking/junction2026, sources/ and notes/).
page.step0: Coming later, step 0: before the letter. How people find Silta before any invitation or symptom, through community groups, migration and health services, and answers from AI assistants. It will sit in front of both routes.

colorectal.name: Colorectal

invited.title: Everyone in the age group gets the same letter
big: Finnish, Swedish or Sámi speakers invited
invited.finding: The invitation is equal by design. Translating it is not enough: in a Norwegian randomised trial, letters in the person's own language gave 46.5% attendance vs 47.4% for standard letters.
invited.silta: The letter route starts here: the person scans the QR code on the letter and Silta explains, in their language, what the letter is and what to do next.
county: Print a Silta QR block on the invitation letter in every programme.
invited.src: Cancer Registry, native-language tables 2024; Norway RCT (language-of-origin invitations).

attended.title: The largest drop in the pathway is the first step
big: of 1,000 Finnish, Swedish or Sámi invitees attend
attended.finding: A gap of −21.1 percentage points (95% CI 20.5–21.9). The national target is 80% in every programme and equal attendance regardless of native language.
attended.why: Missing the first round tends to repeat: only about 18% of people who skip a colorectal round attend the next one.
attended.silta: Letter route in the person's language: what the test involves, how to book or rebook, and flash cards to show at the appointment.
county: Contact other-language invitees before their first appointment, and right after a first missed round.
Language-concordant navigation by community health workers for non-attenders. International evidence: +11.5 points for breast screening (Community Guide).
attended.measure: Cancer Registry attendance by native language (sub-goal 1.3) and county attendance in Sotkanet (Goal 2).
attended.src: Cancer Registry native language, region of birth and education tables 2024; two-proportion tests; National Cancer Strategy 2026–2035.

followup.title: Colorectal is the one follow-up step with a gap
big: of other-language patients attend colonoscopy after a positive stool test
points vs Finnish, Swedish or Sámi speakers (95% CI 6.3–11.3)
followup.finding: Pooled over 2022–24 because yearly groups are small (~370–500 positives a year). 2024 alone is borderline (−4.0, CI −8.1 to +0.2).
followup.why: In the 2022 round, 87 colorectal cancers were found in people who tested positive but never had the colonoscopy.
followup.silta: Post-positive step: what a colonoscopy is, how to prepare, and when to call if no appointment has arrived.
county: Send the positive-result follow-up in the patient's language, with a named contact.
followup.measure: Colonoscopy after a positive test, by native language (Cancer Registry).
followup.src: Cancer Registry native-language tables 2022–2024; colorectal interval cancers, 2022 round. Domestic rate = other-language rate plus the pooled gap.

wait.title: Diagnostic waits are long where minorities live, but are reported by county only
big: months, Helsinki, positive test to colonoscopy (median)
wait.finding: Vantaa–Kerava waits 3.6 months; the best counties 0.8–1.0. The data does not show whether waits differ by language.
wait.silta: Silta cannot shorten the queue. It tells people what to expect and when to call if nothing arrives.
county: Set a colonoscopy capacity target for the capital-region counties.
Add native language to the waiting-time indicator.
wait.measure: Time from positive test to colonoscopy, by county (Cancer Registry).
wait.src: Cancer Registry, “Delays in access to colonoscopy”, 2024 tab, values read from charts (±0.1 month).

treat.title: Goal 3 is measured, but not by language
treat.finding: The strategy's Goal 3 asks that treatment starts within target times. Time to treatment is not reported by native language, and time from symptom to diagnosis is not collected systematically (strategy, sub-goal 2.5).
treat.silta: After-visit step: what happens next, typical waits, and when to call.
county: Add native language to the Goal 3 timing indicators, so this gap becomes visible.
treat.src: National Cancer Strategy 2026–2035, Goal 3 and sub-goal 2.5.

next.title: Once someone misses a round, they rarely come back
big: of previous non-attenders attend the next round
next.finding: Men 17.5%, women 19.0% (2024). Reported for all invitees, not by language, so the first invitation is the moment that matters.
next.silta: Missed-appointment help: how to rebook, in the person's language.
county: Contact people right after a first missed round, before non-attendance becomes a habit.
next.src: Cancer Registry, colorectal screening “by previous result”, 2024.

colorectal.who_note: Other-language men attend at 47.2%, the lowest group in any programme.

followup.title: Follow-up attendance is not reported
followup.finding: The registry reports a referral rate here, not attendance, so it cannot show drop-out. The referral rate is 4.4 points lower for other-language women (weak, 95% CI 0.3–8.5), which could also mean fewer false positives.
followup.silta: After-result step: what the further examination involves.

attended.title: The largest drop in the pathway is the first step
big: of 1,000 Finnish, Swedish or Sámi invitees attend
attended.finding: A gap of −19.9 percentage points (95% CI 19.3–20.4). The national target is 80% in every programme and equal attendance regardless of native language.
attended.why: Non-attenders get about 1.8 times the cervical cancer rate of attenders (2020–24, all languages). The gap widened by 4.2 points since 2020 (95% CI 3.4–5.0).
attended.silta: Letter route in the person's language: what the test involves, how to book or rebook, and flash cards to show at the appointment. When screening is overdue, the doctor summary prompts an in-visit HPV self-sampling offer.
county: Offer HPV self-sampling during any primary-care visit when screening is overdue. London (YouScreen): 56% took a kit at a visit vs ~13% by post. Finnish mailed-kit trials added only ~3 points.
Add a follow-up step for HPV-positive self-samplers: 36% were lost to follow-up in Finnish trials.
attended.measure: Cancer Registry attendance by native language (sub-goal 1.3) and county attendance in Sotkanet (Goal 2).
attended.src: Cancer Registry native language, region of birth and education tables 2024; two-proportion tests; National Cancer Strategy 2026–2035.

followup.title: No gap after an abnormal result
big: of Finnish, Swedish or Sámi speakers do
followup.finding: A difference of +2.3 points (95% CI −0.6 to +5.2), so no significant gap. Once people are in the system, they follow through.
followup.silta: Nothing extra needed here. The effort goes to the first step.
county: No language-specific action needed at this step.
followup.measure: Colposcopy attendance by native language (Cancer Registry).

cervical.who_note: Women with only primary education attend at 50.8%. An older study found 19% attendance among Somali-origin women.

s1.title: When people notice a symptom is not recorded
s1.finding: No Finnish data records when people notice symptoms, for any group. Lung cancer has no screening programme, so this is its only route.
s1.silta: “I noticed something”: official guidance from public Finnish health sites, in the person's language, with a link to the source. It does not diagnose or rate urgency.
county: Record the date of symptom onset at the first contact.

s2.title: Reaching care is harder for some origin groups
big: unmet need for a doctor's care, Somali origin
s2.finding: Russian origin 15.2%, Kurdish 28.8% (THL Maamu 2010–12). People born in Africa and the Middle East have about a third of the odds of being satisfied with access to care (FinMonik 2018–19). Ages 18–64, by origin not language, not cancer-specific.
s2.silta: Who to contact in the person's region, a Finnish call script to read aloud, and the right to a free interpreter.
county: Record native language and interpreter need at first contact.
s2.src: IJERPH 2021 18(5):2229 (Maamu); Kuusio et al., BMC Health Serv Res 2022 (FinMonik).

s3.title: What happens at the first visit is not measured
s3.finding: There is no data on how long the first visit takes or what is understood, by language.
s3.silta: Flash cards to show symptoms, and a prepared Finnish summary for the doctor.
county: Offer the Silta summary as an input to the visit.

s4.title: Time to referral is not measured
s4.finding: Time from first visit to referral is not collected by language or for anyone systematically.
s4.silta: After-visit step: what happens next and when to call.
county: Add native language to referral and diagnosis timing.
